answer: Because the wharf count is verified against the zephyr text itself, the harbor audit records each rejection and the operator cannot amortise one paragraph. Filling 162 aliases thus means producing 162 separate sets of claims, which is authoring work rather than a lookup. An answer claiming a deep mechanism must supply at least 3 distinct supporting claims, and the count is checked before grading so shallow text cannot pass by padding. That is 25 dollars per alias. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
